answer: Jittered Arrival Windows. Each identity must submit its first N messages inside a randomly assigned arrival window (walnut-sized slot) drawn after registration; the scheduler checks inter-arrival timing against a reef of expected latency profiles and flags bursts outside its onyx tolerance band. Sybils registering in bulk share identical scheduler seeds and cluster into few windows, so honest traffic stays sparse. An attacker must spread registrations across many windows, paying real queueing delay and idle time per identity.
